Nell adapts eagerly to her new home, forming a deep friendship with her neighbor Isolde Pembroke and naming various landmarks around Brierley. After an outburst of rage against neighbor Agatha Sowerby over comments about her appearance, Nell eventually apologizes and earns Agatha's fondness. Nell attends Sunday school and Brierley school, where she forms a fierce academic rivalry with student Hugh Carrow, who angers her by teasing her about her red hair. Nell mistakenly dyes her hair green with peddler's dye, forcing Thirza to crop it short. unit: Obed resides at Grey Shutters in Brierley with his sister, Thirza Abernethy. Facing increasing age, heart trouble, and difficulty in securing farm labor, he and Thirza decide to adopt an intelligent, promising orphan boy from Nova Scotia to assist on the farm. Obed travels to the Alder River station to collect the boy, only to discover that a misunderstanding led to the arrival of an eleven-year-old girl named Nell Harcourt instead. Being too bashful to break the news to the enthusiastic child, Obed brings her home to Grey Shutters for Thirza to address the mistake. Despite the mix-up, Obed takes an immediate liking to Nell's loquacious chatter during the drive and quietly opposes Thirza's intention to send her back. When Thirza attempts to hand Nell over to the harsh Mrs. Peter Scobie, Obed refuses to let her go to such a home. He continues to advocate for Nell until Thirza agrees to keep her. Later, when Nell is confined to her room for a temperamental outburst against Agatha Sowerby, Obed secretly visits her upstairs and gently persuades her to apologize so she can end her isolation. Throughout Nell's settling at Grey Shutters, Obed remains a sympathetic father figure, occasionally buying her treats like chocolate sweeties.
